LocalMe HTTP API

Every hosted project talks to the same REST surface. The platform resolves which project is calling from the request path or the X-Project-Id header, so your frontend can use relative /api/… URLs from any page.

JSON over HTTPS
cookie or X-API-Key
no build step

Overview

A project is a folder of static files plus a managed backend: a document database, blob storage, a shared asset library, visitor accounts and roles, routing, encrypted secrets, a reverse proxy, scheduled tasks, webhooks and custom domains. You write HTML, CSS and JavaScript; the platform owns everything else.

<!-- index.html — the whole integration is a fetch call -->
<script>
  const res = await fetch('/api/db/find', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    credentials: 'include',              // sends the visitor cookie
    body: JSON.stringify({ table: 'notes', filter: { done: false } })
  });
  const { data, total } = await res.json();
</script>

Addressing & project context

Projects are served from http://localhost:3000/[username]/[project-name]/. Relative API paths inside a served page inherit that context automatically. Server-side or external clients can address a project explicitly:

POST http://localhost:3000/api/db/find
X-Project-Id: <projectId>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "table": "notes" }

Resolution order is: the X-Project-Id header, an explicit projectId field in the body, then the /username/project/ prefix of the request path.

Authentication

Three credential types reach the API, and they can be combined inside one project:

Visitor session

Cookie auth_<projectId>, issued by /auth/token. Carries the visitor's role and permissions.

API key

Sent as X-API-Key for storage and library operations only — never the database.

Owner or admin

A console session visiting its own project is treated as the Owner role, so everything is permitted.

Login and signup are handled for you. Point visitors at /auth/login?returnUrl=/your/page and upload a login.html at the project root to replace the built-in page with your own design.

await fetch('/auth/token', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    action: 'login',            // or 'signup'
    username: 'jane',
    password: 'hunter2hunter2',
    captcha: answerFromTheSvg,  // required for login
    returnUrl: location.pathname
  })
});
// → { success: true, projectId, visitorId, role, token }
MethodPathNotes
GET
/auth/captcha
public
Returns an SVG math challenge and sets the captcha cookie.
GET
/auth/login?returnUrl=…
public
Built-in login page, or your login.html when present.
POST
/auth/token
public
Log in or sign up a visitor; sets auth_{projectId}.
GET
/auth/me
public
Current principal, role and permission list.
GET
/auth/logout?returnUrl=…
public
Clears the visitor cookie and redirects.

Check who is signed in at any time with /auth/me, which returns the role, the permission list and the principal kind (visitor, api_key, owner or anonymous).

Database

A schema-less document store. Tables are created implicitly on first insert, and every document must carry a non-null id field that is unique inside its table. Queries support a MongoDB-style filter and sort grammar.

MethodPathNotes
POST
/api/db/find
session or API key
Query documents with filter, sort, limit and offset.
POST
/api/db/insert
session or API key
Insert one document. The id field is mandatory and unique per table.
POST
/api/db/update
session or API key
Update matching documents, all of them unless many: false.
POST
/api/db/delete
session or API key
Delete every document matching the filter.
// Query
const res = await fetch('/api/db/find', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    table: 'orders',
    filter: { status: { $in: ['paid', 'shipped'] }, total: { $gt: 100 } },
    sort: { created: -1 },
    limit: 25,
    offset: 0
  })
});
// → { data: [...], total, limit, offset, truncated }
// Insert, update and delete
await fetch('/api/db/insert', {
  method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ table: 'orders', document: { id: Date.now(), total: 140, status: 'paid' } })
});

await fetch('/api/db/update', {
  method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ table: 'orders', filter: { id: 1 }, update: { status: 'shipped' }, many: false })
});

await fetch('/api/db/delete', {
  method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ table: 'orders', filter: { status: 'cancelled' } })
});
OperatorMeaning
$eqequal
$nenot equal
$gt / $gtegreater than (or equal)
$lt / $lteless than (or equal)
$in / $ninmember of an array (or not)
$regexregular expression match
$existsfield is present
$and / $or / $notlogical composition

Updates accept either a plain object (merged into each document) or operator form with $set, $inc and $unset. Results carry _localme metadata with the created and updated timestamps.

Storage

Files are served from your project root, so /static/app.js works exactly as it would on any static host. Binary files live in blob storage; text files are stored inline and editable in the dashboard.

MethodPathNotes
GET
/api/storage/list?path=/
session or API key
List the files in one directory.
GET
/api/storage/status
session or API key
Bytes used, project allocation and file count.
POST
/api/storage/upload
session or API key
Multipart with a file field, or a raw body with ?path= and ?filename=.
GET
/api/storage/download?path=/index.html
session or API key
Stream a stored file.
POST
/api/storage/delete
session or API key
Delete one file by path.
// Multipart upload
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', input.files[0]);
form.append('path', '/static/logo.png');

await fetch('/api/storage/upload', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'X-API-Key': 'sk_…' },   // or credentials: 'include'
  body: form
});

Listing accepts a directory: GET /api/storage/list?path=/static returns names, sizes, modification times and types. Writes that would exceed the account cap are rejected before any bytes are stored.

Library

The library holds assets shared by every project you own — stylesheets, scripts, fonts, images. Reference them at /library/<name> from any project; HTML files are not allowed.

MethodPathNotes
GET
/api/lib/list
session or API key
List every shared asset for the project owner.
GET
/api/lib/status
session or API key
Library usage for the owner.
POST
/api/lib/upload
session or API key
Upload a non-HTML asset into the shared library.
POST
/api/lib/delete
session or API key
Remove a shared asset by name.
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/library/theme.css">
<script src="/library/analytics.js" defer></script>

Secrets & the reverse proxy

Secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and only decrypted server-side. The supported way to use a third-party API without exposing your key is a proxy route: create a route whose path is your own, point it at the provider, and reference secrets in the header map.

// Route:  /api/payments/create    (proxy enabled)
// Target: https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents
// Method: POST
// Headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer {{STRIPE_KEY}}" }

const res = await fetch('/api/payments/create', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 1000, currency: 'usd' })
});

Header values support {{KEY_NAME}} substitution for any stored secret. Secrets can also be read directly with POST /api/secrets/get, which requires the secrets_admin permission and is intended for server-to-server calls only.

Routing & serving

An incoming request is resolved in this order:

  1. An exact route match serves its target HTML file.
  2. A wildcard route match (for example /blog/*) serves its target.
  3. A stored file at the requested path is served directly with long-lived caching.
  4. <dir>/index.html is served for directory paths.
  5. /404.html is returned with status 404, or the platform page.

Routes can require a signed-in visitor and a minimum role. Only HTML files are routable — assets are always reachable by their own path. When the watermark is enabled the platform appends a small attribution badge to served HTML, which you can turn off per project in Settings.

Scheduled tasks and webhooks

Five cron jobs ship with every project (session cleanup, log retention, daily stats, daily summary, orphaned upload cleanup) and can be toggled or run on demand from the dashboard. Webhooks POST a signed JSON payload for project, user, storage and cron events; verify x-webhook-signature using the secret you configured.

Limits & quotas

5 MB account storage

Shared by every project plus the library. Writes past the cap fail with 402 before data is written.

10 MB per file

Hard ceiling on a single upload, multipart or raw body.

500 documents per query

The page size is capped at 500 and the platform scans at most 5000 documents per request, flagging truncated when it hits that bound.

100 free visits per project / month

Only HTML page serves count. Assets, 404s and 403s are free, refreshes inside five minutes are deduplicated, and the counter resets on the first of the month.

Rate limits

Per-identity sliding windows protect each route group; exceeding one returns 429 with Retry-After.

Session lifetime

Console sessions slide on activity and expire after 20 idle minutes. Visitor cookies last 20 minutes and are scoped to their project.

Errors

Failures use standard status codes and a consistent JSON body:

{ "error": "A document with id \"1\" already exists in orders", "code": "duplicate_document_id" }
StatusCommon codes
400invalid_json, invalid_document, missing_document_id, reserved_path, invalid_target
401unauthenticated — sign in or attach credentials
402visit allowance exhausted for the month, or storage cap exceeded
403forbidden — missing permission, disabled endpoint, or blocked hotlink
404not_found — no route, file or record matched
409duplicate_document_id, table_exists, route_exists, domain_exists, project_exists
413file_too_large — the 10 MB per-file ceiling
429rate_limit_exceeded — inspect the Retry-After header
500internal_error — the platform logged the failure for review
